text:
A small amount of air is introduced into the vacuum above the mercury in a mercury barometer
tube.
The mercury level goes down.
Why does the mercury level go down?
A
The air molecules cool the mercury and make it contract.
B
The air molecules decrease the pressure above the mercury.
C
The air molecules heat the mercury and make it expand.
D
The air molecules increase the pressure above the mercury.

options.label: A
options.text: The air molecules cool the mercury and make it contract.

options.label: B
options.text: The air molecules decrease the pressure above the mercury.

options.label: C
options.text: The air molecules heat the mercury and make it expand.

options.label: D
options.text: The air molecules increase the pressure above the mercury.
